response.answer: Maksud Ali PhD critiques governmental rationalities in English-in-education policy, focusing on misrecognition and social equity. He argues that such policies often neglect social struggles and perpetuate inequality. His work emphasizes the need for an ideological perspective in language policy research.

results.content: Ali, M.M., Hamid, M.O. Governmental rationalities and misrecognising human and social conditions in English-in-education policy for individual and social development. • This article provides fresh perspectives in language policy research to critique development in relation to language-in-education policy (LEP) in developing countries. • LEP is a key tool for human capital development. • Sen’s conceptualisation of development is dominant in language policy/education research, but we find this idea problematic as Sen is complicit to human capital theory/ neoliberalism. • Ideological perspective is important to unpack the politics of development discourses and how these are used to govern populations in interested ways. • Misrecognition is central to governing neoliberal citizens and how unequal social struggles over linguistic human capital development are accepted as natural.
